newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki falls in vacant trade after U.S. tumble.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki falls in vacant trade after U.S. tumble.

text.p: Shares sagged all session on Monday in very thin trade after a steep slide in U.S. stocks on Friday, brokers said. Trade was thin with no panic but no buying interest either, they said.
"There weren't any buyers in this market since they could buy just about any share they wanted at a lower price tomorrow," one broker said.

Volume was just 320 million markka with some 40 percent in Nokia, and the HEX general index closed off 1.62 percent at 2,766.42 points. The FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark dipped 1.91 percent to 960.18.
Bourse engine Nokia first fell to around 297.20 -- the equivalent of its close in the U.S. -- but extended losses in late dealings to end down 6.00 markka or 2.00 percent at 294.00.
Forestries underperformed with an almost three percent fall, tracking a similar pattern abroad, where U.S. paper stocks fell even more sharply than the Dow on Friday, brokers said.
Pharma distributor Tamro fell 0.10 markka to 32.60 -- a clear outperformance -- amid big in-house trades which brokers said pointed towards foreign interest. Volume was almost 17 million markka.

Steel group Rautaruukki fell 1.20 markka or 2.68 percent to 43.60 markka after announcing an offering of 32 million shares but brokers said it held up rather well considering the coming dilution from 13 million new shares to be issued.
Brokers said near-term focus would be on U.S. March CPI data due on Tuesday at 1230 GMT/1330 GMT, which is forecast to show a 0.2 percent rise compared to 0.3 percent in February.
